findings.title: Repair pending expert pointer tables before allowing a retry to execute

sources.symbol: executeCompiled1705: AdvanceExperts failure returns; persistent resources retained

findings.evidence: advance clears mapped route flags before promotion. demote changes host pointers; promote overwrites a victim's card slot with another expert. Final publish(ctx) can fail/cancel after that copy, leaving bank.changed true and an old device pointer at overwritten bytes. With flags clear, next advance returns nil before publish, so executeCompiled can run with stale expert identities. The promote-error branch attempts noncancelable publication, but failure there has the same retry hole. Existing table injects first-copy/pinning/early-cancel errors, not failed final publication with retry. New graph replay leaves this predicate unchanged.
findings.impact: A request cancellation or table-write failure can leave retained expert resources unsafe for the next request; a successful retry may read another expert's weights. Source-confirmed recovery path; no observed incorrect output or measured incident claimed.
findings.recommended_change: Use existing bank.changed/publish ownership to ensure every successful advance, including the no-route branch, has repaired pending tables before kernels run. A failed repair must continue to refuse execution. Preserve noncancelable cleanup, mapping/slot identities and lifetime; no second state ledger or fallback execution path.
findings.displaced_surface: Remove the unconditional no-route success that bypasses outstanding publication. Extend the existing failed-promotion subtest and readable assertion; keep one fixture/fake memory owner. Retain card/host split, miss/hit, capacity, release and CUDA bit-equivalence tests; no existing test deletion justified.
findings.likely_effort: Small local recovery repair plus existing-fixture cases; independent of graph-capture optimization.

expected_benefit.outcome: Prevents reuse of stale expert mappings after interruption through the existing dirty-table owner.

findings.title: Charge the GGUF sampling budget before allocating and reading its samples

sources.symbol: openGGUF 13 already serves budget/spectral tests via testutil.TempGGUF

findings.evidence: MeasureGGUF calls sampleGGUFTensorValues before meter.charge(bytesNeeded). That helper computes geometry, allocates float64 samples and block buffers, then reads/dequantizes every sampled block. An exhausted --max-read therefore refuses only after the offending tensor's sampling work. Safetensors sampling and collectMatrixSpectrum already precharge. Existing budget test checks the returned error but cannot distinguish pre-read from post-read refusal. Successful documents still account reads correctly; no corrupt evidence or measured incident is asserted.
findings.impact: A declared read ceiling fails to bound work on the failure path. Default 4096 samples bounds the overshoot to one tensor's sampled storage (F32 16 KiB); a caller can raise samples independently of max-read and force much larger reads and float64 allocation before refusal. No full-store or model benchmark was run.
findings.recommended_change: At sampleGGUFTensorValues' checked-geometry boundary, charge existing readMeter before allocations/reads; compute geometry once. Keep spectral precharge exactly once. Strengthen TestMeasurementChargesReadBudget's rejection case to observe no tensor read. Replace deterministic sampling test's manual Create/Write/Close/Open with existing openGGUF, preserving values/assertions.
findings.displaced_surface: Remove post-read sample charging/unused byte-return plumbing and deterministic test's manual write/open/error/cleanup sequence. Keep budget/spectral, identity, sample/IQR, codec, Safetensors and document-validation contracts. Existing openGGUF already serves budget/spectral callers; no exported reader API, framework, fixture/schema/gate.

device_newton_schulz_normalization.assessment: All owner refinements were applied before the deciding comparison. Supported Windows/CUDA execution required OVERGO_CUDA_TEST=1 and observed execution of both 8+2 FP32 and 4+2 TF32. The 514 scalar comparisons and 56 directions passed bitwise, including guard decisions, normalization multipliers, zero/tiny weights and thresholds around rounded FP32 squared norms. FP64 round-to-nearest scalar instructions were checked despite fast-math compiler options. Twelve alternating pairs across 32 cells compared preservation with reconstruction and counted bandwidth, launches and otherwise-skipped GEMMs. Normal cases ranged from no detectable gain to about 15% faster; every guarded cell was about 105-395% slower. The declared stopping rule rejected the candidate before further full-step/streamed runs. The unchanged production path remains. Optimizer-only gain could have qualified under the frozen 5% minimum, full-step regression and memory limits, but the guard-heavy limit failed. No candidate full-step improvement is claimed.
